## 1. Historical Context

### 1.1 Timeline of Key Developments

```
1958: Perceptron (Rosenblatt) - Single neuron, linear separation
1960s: Adaline (Widrow-Hoff) - First learning rule using gradient descent
1969: Minsky & Papert - "Perceptrons" book exposes limitations of single-layer networks
1974: Paul Werbos - First description of backpropagation in PhD thesis
1986: Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams - Popularizes backpropagation
1989: LeCun - Backpropagation applied to CNNs
1998: LeNet-5 - Handwritten digit recognition
2012: AlexNet - Revives deep learning, wins ImageNet
2015+: Modern era - Transformers, massive models, autodiff frameworks
```

### 1.2 Key Figures

| Researcher | Year | Contribution |
|------------|------|--------------|
| Frank Rosenblatt | 1958 | Perceptron algorithm |
| Bernard Widrow | 1960 | Adaline, LMS rule |
| Paul Werbos | 1974 | Backpropagation (thesis) |
| David Rumelhart | 1986 | Popularized backpropagation |
| Geoffrey Hinton | 1986 | Co-developed backprop |
| Yann LeCun | 1989 | Backprop in CNNs |
| Sergey Ioffe | 2015 | Batch Normalization |

### 1.3 Why Backpropagation Matters

Before backpropagation, neural networks were limited to single layers because:
- No efficient method to compute gradients for multi-layer networks
- Learning was too slow for practical applications
- XOR problem couldn't be solved

Backpropagation solved all three by enabling:
- Efficient gradient computation in O(w) time (w = number of weights)
- Learning in deep architectures
- Practical training of non-linear functions

---

## 2. The Forward Pass

### 2.1 Network Architecture

Consider a simple feedforward network:

```
Input (x) → Linear → Activation → Linear → Activation → ... → Output (ŷ)
            W₁, b₁                 W₂, b₂
```

### 2.2 Mathematical Representation

For a network with L layers:

```
z¹ = x · W¹ + b¹        # Layer 1 pre-activation
a¹ = σ(z¹)              # Layer 1 activation

z² = a¹ · W² + b²       # Layer 2 pre-activation  
a² = σ(z²)              # Layer 2 activation

...

zᴸ = a⁽ᴸ⁻¹⁾ · Wᴸ + bᴸ  # Output layer pre-activation
ŷ = σ(zᴸ)               # Output (or softmax for classification)
```

Where:
- x ∈ ℝ^(batch_size × input_dim)
- Wˡ ∈ ℝ^(n_{l-1} × n_l) - weight matrix
